title: C++ Quiz
description: Review the ideas from the lessons. Take your time. After each answer, read the note that explains the rule. You can try again.

questions.question: What does a C++ compiler do?
questions.explanation: You write the source code. The compiler translates it and reports many mistakes before the program runs.
options: Turns source code into a program
Changes the colour of the screen
Stores every program on the web

questions.question: Fill the gap: g++ ___ hello.cpp -o hello selects the C++20 rules.
questions.explanation: The -std flag chooses the language version. These examples use C++20.

questions.question: Why does this line fail to compile?
questions.explanation: Braces stop this change because 3.5 would lose its .5 part. Use double when you need a decimal.
options: An int cannot keep the fractional part

questions.question: What type does auto name = "Asha"; choose?
questions.explanation: A text literal becomes a pointer to constant characters here. Use std::string name = "Asha"; for a string object.

questions.question: Which word usually stops a switch case from continuing into the next case? ___
questions.explanation: break leaves the switch. Without it, the next case can run too.

questions.question: Which pair can be two overloads of add?
questions.explanation: An overload is another function with the same name but different input types or input counts.
options: Two functions with the same inputs and only different return types

questions.question: What does int value() const promise?
questions.explanation: The const after the method inputs says it can read the object without changing its ordinary fields.
options: This method will not change ordinary fields of the object

questions.question: What does override help C++ check?
questions.explanation: override catches mistakes such as spelling a method name wrong. The child must match a virtual method from the parent.
options: That every object has the same name
That a child method matches a virtual parent method

questions.question: Fill the gap: ___ <typename T> starts a function recipe for different types.
questions.explanation: A template leaves a place for a type. C++ fills in that place when the recipe is used.

questions.question: How many items does this vector have?
questions.explanation: The vector starts with two items. push_back adds one more at the end.

questions.question: Which lambda is true when a number is greater than five?
questions.explanation: The > sign means greater than. For example, 8 > 5 is true.

questions.question: You should call delete yourself on the object owned by a unique_ptr.
questions.explanation: The unique_ptr cleans up the object it owns. Deleting that object yourself can cause a second, invalid delete.

questions.question: What does std::string("Hi, ") + "Asha" make?
questions.explanation: The + sign joins the pieces of text. The first piece already contains the comma and space.
options: HiAsha with no space or comma

questions.question: Fill the gap: score.___(0) reads an optional score or uses 0 if it is empty.
questions.explanation: value_or uses the stored value when present. Otherwise it returns the fallback you supplied.
